## Fixed: YouTube and other video sites

- **Downloads failed with an error.** YouTube now needs a JavaScript runtime next to yt-dlp, and NDM only installed yt-dlp. **Downloads → Set yt-dlp** now also installs [Deno](https://deno.com) (checked against its release's SHA-256, kept up to date like yt-dlp) and hands it to yt-dlp. Choose **Set yt-dlp** once more after updating.
- **Best quality without ffmpeg.** Without ffmpeg, NDM used to ask yt-dlp for a single file with both picture and sound, which YouTube only has in low quality, if at all. Now NDM downloads the best video and the best audio and joins them itself into one MP4 (or WebM). With ffmpeg installed, yt-dlp joins them as before.
- **"Download this video" on the player did nothing on YouTube.** The panel only saw the pieces YouTube's player streams, which aren't the video. On YouTube and the other video sites it now sends the page to NDM, like the right-click menu item, and says "Sent to New Download Manager".
- When yt-dlp can't get a video, the Download File Info window now shows yt-dlp's own message (for example "needs signing in") instead of just "Error". The video is named after its title and goes to the Video category.
- YouTube downloads no longer send your browser's YouTube cookies to yt-dlp; signed-in, yt-dlp finds fewer formats.
- Set yt-dlp no longer depends on GitHub's release web pages; it compares the release checksums with the installed copies.

Reload the extension in your browser (its extensions page → reload, or load the exported folder again) to get the panel fix.
